newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan state fund asked to sell bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan state fund asked to sell bank shares.

text.p: A parliamentary sub-committee said on Wednesday it had ordered a cabinet development fund to sell its stakes in three financial institutions in two years.
The cabinet's fund had a total of T$7.586 billion investments in the International Commercial Bank of China, China Bills Finance and unlisted Overseas Chinese Bank.
"The investments are inconsistent to the development fund's establishment purpose," a lawmaker said of the committee's resolution, broadcast on state-funded television.
"The fund should withdraw its investments in two years," the lawmaker said.
The cabinet fund was aimed at helping upgrade local industries and it was inappropriate to invest in financial sector, the lawmaker said.
The committee's resolution needs final approval from the entire parliament.
Finance Minister Paul Chiu said his ministry would fully respect parliament's decision, but added these shares should be released gradually to reduce the impact on the stock market.

The fund had invested T$4.588 billion in the International Commercial Bank of China, T$1.122 billion in China Bills Finance and T$1.876 billion in the Overseas Chinese Bank, state-funded Central News Agency reported.

The agency did not give the fund's current stakes in the three financial institutions, but said the fund has proposed to cut its investments in the International Commercial Bank of China to 850 million shares or 41.76 percent of the bank's total stake by the end of fiscal 1997/98 (July/June).
It planned to hold 165 million shares or 16.55 percent in China Bills Finance and 176 million shares or 14.08 percent in Overseas Chinese Bank by 1997/98.
On Wednesday, the International Commercial Bank of China was down 50 cents or 0.68 percent to T$73 and China Bills fell 10 cents to T$27.
